NC-NULL-OVERLAP-0.observed: FP = 0.0042 at threshold 0.20 (1 false positive out of 240 noise samples)
NC-NULL-OVERLAP-0.note: Near-zero; 1 FP out of 240 is within sampling noise

PC-FP-BINDING-100.description: At 100% overlap, FP at threshold 0.20 must exceed 0.20

C3-ORTHOGONALITY-50.note: Orthogonality fails at 50% overlap — behavioral score becomes correlated with structural signal

CONTINUOUS-INJECTION.description: Unique behavioral scores >= 5 at all conditions

observations: Gaussian overlap design achieved empirical overlap close to targets: 0.42% vs 0% target at 0%; 23.75% vs 25% at 25%; 44.17% vs 50% at 50%; 67.5% vs 75% at 75%; 96.25% vs 100% at 100%.

Calibrated threshold increases among conditions with valid thresholds: 0.20 (0%) -> 0.25 (25%) -> 0.27 (50%). This confirms the hypothesis that threshold increases gradually under genuine overlap, unlike the parent's flat-then-jump pattern.

At 75% and 100% overlap, no valid calibrated threshold exists (None). No threshold in the 50-point grid [0.05, ..., 0.54] satisfies both TPR>=0.85 and FPR<=0.10. This means the freshness guard CANNOT simultaneously maintain high detection rate and low false positive rate at high overlap.
FP at baseline threshold 0.20 increases monotonically with overlap: 0.42% -> 23.75% -> 44.17% -> 67.5% -> 96.25%. The FP binding below 75% is confirmed (FP > 0 at 25% and 50%).

Orthogonality (TOST delta=0.15) FAILS at 50% overlap: Pearson r=0.080, CI upper=0.168 > 0.15. This means at 50% overlap, the behavioral freshness score becomes correlated with the structural signal, violating the orthogonality assumption.
Orthogonality holds at 0% (r=-0.023, CI=0.066), 25% (r=-0.029, CI=0.061), 75% (r=0.046, CI=0.135), and 100% (r=-0.026, CI=0.064). The 50% condition is the only failure.
C1 structural discrimination is 0.8333 across all conditions (4 auth states, 3 unique fingerprints), consistent with parent experiment.
Continuous injection check passes: 452-460 unique behavioral scores per condition (well above the minimum of 5).

The run_experiment.py code computed overall_hypothesis_outcome as HYPOTHESIS_SUPPORTED, but this does not apply the full frozen decision rule from spec.json. The spec.json decision_rule falsifies when orthogonality breaks at any condition (condition (c)), which occurs at 50% overlap.
validity_notes: Decision rule discrepancy: The run_experiment.py internally computed HYPOTHESIS_SUPPORTED based on monotonicity and FP binding criteria only. However, the frozen spec.json decision_rule states the claim is FALSIFIED if orthogonality breaks at any condition (condition (c)). The prereg.md also states FALSIFIED if calibrated_threshold is None at any condition (step 4). This result.json applies the frozen decision rule correctly, overriding the code's internal assessment.

The calibrated threshold being None at 75% and 100% overlap is NOT a measurement failure — it is a valid scientific finding. It means no operating point exists that satisfies both TPR>=0.85 and FPR<=0.10 at those overlap levels.

The 50% overlap condition is borderline: calibrated threshold exists (0.27) and FP binding is clear (44.17%), but orthogonality fails marginally (CI upper 0.168 vs delta 0.15). With 480 samples, this is a real effect, not a power issue.
Gaussian design limitation: production noise distributions may not be Gaussian. This tests the principle of genuine overlap, not production fidelity.
Clamping artifact: Gaussian samples clamped to [0,1] slightly reduced effective overlap at extreme conditions (e.g., 0% overlap measured as 0.42% because some noise samples clamped upward).

Parent experiment (EXP-PRODUCT-35551517868) used uniform-shift overlap which produced 0% actual overlap at 25%/50% conditions. This experiment's Gaussian design fixed that flaw — empirical overlap at 25%/50% is now 23.75%/44.17% respectively.
The raw evidence file (experiment_data.json) contains full threshold sweep data for all 5 conditions, per-condition behavioral/structural statistics, and Phase C raw discrimination probes.
unresolved: Why does orthogonality fail specifically at 50% overlap but not at 75% or 100%? The 50% condition has r=0.080 while 75% has r=0.046 and 100% has r=-0.026. This non-monotonic pattern warrants investigation.

Is the calibrated threshold at 50% overlap (0.27) practically usable given the orthogonality failure? The threshold exists but the behavioral-structural correlation at this overlap level may undermine the guard's independence assumption.
Would increasing sample size at 50% overlap (n>=800) change the TOST result? Current CI upper is 0.168 vs delta 0.15 — a 12% overshoot that might缩小 with more data, or might be a stable effect.

The prereg.md step 4 (calibrated_threshold is None -> FALSIFIED) and the spec.json decision_rule (FALSIFIED if orthogonality breaks) are independent falsification paths. Both trigger. Should future preregistrations consolidate these into a single decision tree?

Production relevance: Gaussian overlap is a controlled test of the discrimination principle. Real production noise may have different distributional properties (heavy tails, multimodal, etc.). A follow-up experiment with production-like noise distributions would strengthen the claim.
